evidence.intree_statement: Definition preserves_right_Kan `(R : E ⟶ F) := ∀ C D (G : C ⟶ E) (K : C ⟶ D) `(!RightKan K E) `(!RightKan K F), R ◯ Ran K G ≈ Ran K (R ◯ G).
Definition preserves_left_Kan `(L : E ⟶ F) := ∀ C D (G : C ⟶ E) (K : C ⟶ D) `(!LeftKan K E) `(!LeftKan K F), L ◯ Lan K G ≈ Lan K (L ◯ G).

statement_record.book: Given C -K-> M -T-> A -G-> X and a right Kan extension Ran_K T with counit epsilon, G PRESERVES this right Kan extension when (G o Ran_K T, G(epsilon)) is itself a right Kan extension of GT along K; Mac Lane notes this is STRICTLY STRONGER than the bare isomorphism G o Ran_K T ~= Ran_K(GT).
statement_record.intree: preserves_right_Kan R := for all C D G K with global RightKan on E and F, R ◯ Ran K G ≈ Ran K (R ◯ G)  — where ≈ between functors is natural isomorphism (Functor_Setoid_Nat_Iso, Instance/Fun.v).
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-WEAKER, on two axes. (1) It encodes exactly the bare natural isomorphism R ◯ Ran K G ≅ Ran K (R ◯ G) that Mac Lane explicitly calls out as strictly weaker than genuine preservation; it never asserts the canonical comparison (the whiskered counit G(epsilon)) is the one witnessing the Kan extension. (2) It quantifies over the GLOBAL adjoints RightKan K E, RightKan K F (all extensions along K exist) and is a 'preserves ALL' predicate on R, so it cannot express 'G preserves THIS particular local Ran_K T' — the LocalRightKan record with its counit ran_transform is present but no preservation predicate is defined over it.

gap: The library's preserves_right_Kan captures only the weak bare-natural-iso notion (R ◯ Ran ≅ Ran(R◯−)), not Mac Lane's counit-universality (G ∘ Ran_K T being a Kan extension with counit G·ε). It is also global-only (uses the RightKan adjoint classes, 'preserves all'), with no predicate for preservation of a single specified local Kan extension. Missing: (a) the strong counit-tracking definition; (b) its application to LocalRightKan; (c) the theorem that the two are inequivalent in general.
